newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl wants swift end to Bosnia repatriation row.
newsitem.headline: Kohl wants swift end to Bosnia repatriation row.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl called on Monday for new efforts to end a row over the repatriation of some 320,000 Bosnian refugees taken in by Germany's 16 regional states during the 1992-95 war.

Speaking before a meeting of his Christian Democratic Union party executives in Bonn, Kohl said the government was keen to send the refugees back as quickly as possible if conditions in their home regions allowed it.

A row between German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and the ministers of Germany's states followed the states' decision last year to sanction forcible repatriations if refugees failed to go home of their own accord.
A spokesman for Kinkel said on Monday he was now seeking to hold talks this week with representatives from the states, together with German Interior Minister Manfred Kanther.

Kinkel was earlier quoted in the Hamburger Morgenpost newspaper as saying the refugees could not simply be shipped out of Germany to be left to their fate in a homeland where many regions were not able to take them in.
But German state representatives dismissed Kinkel's position and hinted at apparent differences between his viewpoint and that of Interior Minister Kanther.
"If there was some degree of coordination within the federal government, it would certainly be of some help," Saarland state Interior Minister Herbert Mandelartz said on German radio.
Around 100 Bosnian refugees have been repatriated against their will.
